I have identified the relevant files and am ready to cite the delivery function and protection mechanism.

The outbound delivery executes in the `Post()` function at `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go`. It is invoked asynchronously by `PostAsync()`, which enqueues jobs to worker threads. The actual HTTP request is sent through `safeClient.Do(req)` inside `Post()`.

The protection mechanism is enforced in two layers. `ValidateURL` in `validate.go` rejects URLs that resolve to private or reserved IP ranges during webhook registration. `safeDialContext` in `webhook.go` blocks dial attempts to those same addresses at runtime via the HTTP transport. This prevents SSRF and DNS rebinding attacks against internal networks.

The full picture is now clear.

The outbound delivery executes in `Post` at `internal/webhook/webhook.go` (line 152). It is triggered from `memo_service_webhooks.go` via `webhook.PostAsync`, which queues to workers that call `Post(payload)`. The protection against internal network addresses is `ValidateURL` in `internal/webhook/validate.go`, which rejects URLs resolving to reserved or private IPs.

A second protection layer exists at runtime. `safeDialContext` in `internal/webhook/webhook.go` uses a custom `DialContext` on the HTTP transport to reject reserved or private IPs during hostname resolution. It reuses the `isReservedIP` logic from `validate.go`.

The exact answer is still being weighed. `ValidateURL` in `internal/webhook/validate.go` is the stronger candidate for "what protects it," because it validates URLs at configuration time, while `safeDialContext` only guards at runtime.

The final answer pairs `Post` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go` — with `ValidateURL` — `internal/webhook/validate.go`. The latter is the chosen protection because its header explicitly states that reserved CIDR ranges must never be targeted by outbound webhook requests.

The final answer is `Post` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go`; `safeDialContext` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go`. `safeDialContext` is the chosen protection because the question links it directly to the outbound delivery execution.
